questions.stem: Which of the following are histological features of chronic pancreatitis in the pancreas?
questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above
  • Chronic pancreatitis is a long-term inflammation of the pancreas that results in progressive damage and structural changes.
  • Histologically, chronic pancreatitis exhibits multiple characteristic features, including fibrosis, atrophy and dropout of acini, and dilation of the pancreatic duct.
  • Hence, option D. All of the above is correct.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 683

questions.stemHtml: Based on the histological findings showing dense fibrosis and few remaining atrophic pancreatic acini, what is your diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Chronic pancreatitis
  • The given histological image showing fibrosis, atrophy and dropout of acini, and variable dilation of the pancreatic duct is suggestive of Chronic pancreatitis.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 683

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding congenital cysts of the pancreas except:

options.label: B
options.text: It develops due to anomalous development

options.label: C
options.text: Cyst is lined by columnar epithelium

options.label: D
options.text: Cysts are filled with clear and serous fluid

questions.solutionHtml:
It is multilocular
  • Congenital cyst of the pancreas is a rare condition that typically presents as a single cyst rather than a multilocular lesion.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 683
